Why did E2E QL-to-login fall to 25% from a historic 40%?
Why are repeat partners flat at 52-56 while active partners grew ~25%?

risks: Institutional and E2E still operate as two teams after 1.5 years; the missing single business story is the biggest structural watch item.
Net revenue stuck around 30-40% retention with no visible waterfall - leadership cannot attribute the miss.
High payouts continue to erode NR; incentives are linked to payout, reinforcing the problem.
QL-to-login conversion collapsed from 40% to 25%; RCA and fix are still outstanding.
Headcount 61 vs 77 plan; heavy early-tenure churn; May target of 82 requires adding 21 people by month end.
Repeat partners stagnant (52-56) despite 25% active-partner growth - retention quality concern.
Large-partner and CAMP accounts not structured in CRM - accountability is fragile.
meeting_dynamics: Raghu carried nearly all the probing and the push for structural change; functional leads were largely reactive.
Ishaan's live 2/10 insight rating was the most candid self-assessment in the meeting - acknowledged but not resolved in-room.
The institutional-vs-E2E divide surfaced repeatedly as competing narratives and was deferred to a future restructure.
Joint review and WBR/MBR restructure agreed in principle without a firm owner, format, or transition plan.
Marketing presented output metrics enthusiastically; Raghu redirected to business lift measurement - same pattern as retail review.
Several large-partner and CAM items discussed at length and parked without named owners.
